source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Power on and boot in BIOS.
2. Press load default,save and reboot.
3. Boot in BIOS,compare setting should matches SPEC.
4. Change BIOS all/random setting in this function,to non-default  setting.
5. Save and reboot.
6. Boot in BIOS and check your setting still exist.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. The default setting should matches SPEC."
2. No error log happen.
3. Normal reboot ,no hang、crash happen.
4. Check your set still exist.

original_test_intent: Verify UEFI Variables Protection defaults and approved non-default persistence without allowing unauthorized variable changes or blocking authorized boot entry maintenance, Secure Boot operations, firmware update or recovery.
original_method: Manually Load Default and compare named protection fields with SPEC, then apply bounded non-default values, save/reboot and visually verify persistence while approved read-only variable metadata and non-destructive access behavior are checked.
manual_activity: A security-authorized engineer must interpret and operate the protection fields in pre-OS Setup, perform default/non-default reboot phases and visually accept values. Agent variable metadata collection cannot replace those steps.
required_inputs: Board/BIOS identity and UEFI variable implementation
Named protection fields and affected namespaces/attributes
SPEC defaults and approved non-default values
Allowlisted disposable variable or vendor-approved non-destructive validation
Secure Boot/boot entry/update/recovery dependencies and OOB recovery
safety_requirements: Never operationalize all/random or write/delete boot, Secure Boot, PK/KEK/db/dbx, recovery or vendor-critical variables without separate explicit approval.
Collect names, GUIDs and attributes only unless content is explicitly approved; never expose secrets or key material.
Use a disposable allowlisted test variable when write behavior must be proven.
Stop on unexpected access, denied authorized maintenance, boot/update/recovery failure or variable drift.
agent_execution_scope: Collect read-only variable names/GUIDs/attributes, boot entries, Secure Boot/TPM metadata, firmware identity, logs and BMC health.
Compare only approved non-destructive validation outcomes around operator phases.
Do not drive BIOS, write/delete variables, alter keys or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve protection semantics, variable allowlist, defaults, validation and recovery.
Perform/capture Load Default and bounded non-default persistence phases.
Evaluate authorized/unauthorized access behavior and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correctly refuses agent BIOS operation. No source command exists; direct efivarfs or utility writes are potentially destructive and do not replace the firmware-setting lifecycle.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain the firmware method; add read-only metadata and only a vendor/owner-approved disposable-variable check. Do not propose generic variable-write commands.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The default-first sequence, null script and 5/20-minute fields are retained; all/random is preserved solely as original wording.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Map each protection field to variable namespace and authenticated-write behavior, baseline names/GUIDs/attributes, then test an allowlisted disposable variable for the expected authorized/blocked result while preserving boot/update/recovery paths.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact firmware implementation, boot mode and security enrollment state.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS, bootloader, OS/kernel, Secure Boot/TPM and variable-inspection tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform UEFI Variables Protection documentation and vendor guidance for authenticated variables, update and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces arbitrary mutation with a namespace-specific non-destructive protection check.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; preserves default/persistence coverage and adds scoped enforcement evidence without touching critical variables.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Field/namespace map, disposable variable, defaults and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A disposable-variable result cannot prove every protected namespace; report the exact allowlist and exclusions.

project_override_considerations: The project may validate only selected protection modes and one disposable namespace. Completion must state that scope and must not claim full Secure Boot or firmware-update variable coverage.
expected_evidence: Platform/security identity, field/namespace/default matrix, approval and recovery
Baseline variable names/GUIDs/attributes, boot entries and update/recovery readiness
Load Default captures and SPEC comparison
Non-default persistence plus allowlisted authorized/blocked access result
Final variable/security state, logs and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The default-first and persistence lifecycle agrees with the criteria. The exact namespaces and validation method are project readiness inputs rather than contradictory source facts.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The protection lifecycle is identifiable. Exact semantics, allowlist and recovery are required execution gates but do not make the master case permanently blocked.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Agrees with manual firmware execution and adds variable/security-specific controls.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its recovery and variable metadata improvements while correcting classification to MANUAL ONLY.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates core human acceptance from agent evidence and forbids generic writes to critical UEFI variables.

review_improvement: Defines a safe disposable-variable validation and namespace-specific evidence instead of treating protected firmware variables as generic BIOS settings.
independent_technical_reasoning: The core operations are pre-OS navigation, security-field interpretation and visual verification, all human-owned. Automated metadata collection is collateral evidence, so MANUAL ONLY is required.
no_automatic_retry: Do not repeat protection changes, variable access attempts, defaults or reboot after unexpected behavior; preserve first evidence and obtain security-owner disposition.
